newsitem.title: USA: UN overseers await Iraq price formula, no sign yet.
newsitem.headline: UN overseers await Iraq price formula, no sign yet.

text.p: U.N. oil overseers are expecting, but have not yet received, Iraq's pricing formula for second round "oil-for-food" sales Tuesday morning, according to one of the overseers.
"Well, we are waiting for that, but no, it has not come yet," said a U.N.-appointed oil expert, who wished to remain anonymous.

Once the overseers receive Baghdad's pricing mechanism, the formula is sent with a recommendation to the U.N. sanctions committee, or 661 committee. The overseer said the entire process should take two days, or 48 hours, assuming the formula meets with no objections from oil experts or sanctions committee members.

A Western diplomat on the sanctions panel said the pricing mechanism will be circulated to all 15 committee members under "no-objection procedures," meaning that if no objection is made before a 48-hour limit expires, then the Iraqi formula is approve and oil sales can start.
"Sanctions members will have two days in which to reply. So, if the price formula is submitted today (Tuesday), then you're looking at Thursday or Friday for starting (oil sales)," said the diplomat.
U.N. officials and diplomats expect no delays in implementing the price formula once the Iraqis submit the documentation.
On Monday, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan formally announced approval of Iraq's humanitarian aid distribution plan, freeing Iraq to put forth the pricing formula to trigger oil sales.
Under terms of the oil accord, Iraq is allowed to sell $2.14 billion of oil over 180 days in two equal installments, with the period starting June 8.
